Objective_Text: authorized users are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires a complete inventory of all user accounts in the M365 tenant including regular users, administrators, service accounts, guest users, and shared mailboxes. The list must show account creation dates, last sign-in activity, assigned roles/permissions, account status (enabled/disabled), and business purpose/department. Evidence must demonstrate that only authorized personnel have accounts and that the organization maintains formal processes for account creation, approval, and regular review. The user list must reconcile with HR records and show clear authorization trails.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API can export comprehensive user lists with properties, roles, sign-in activity, and audit trails. Azure AD reports provide user inventory and access reviews.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve complete list of all user accounts with properties
Get users with sign-in activity and account status
List all directory roles for permission mapping
Get members assigned to each administrative role
Retrieve service accounts and application identities
Get audit trail of user account creation/modification
Verify Azure Virtual Desktop service principals for CUI enclave
List AVD host pools used for CUI isolation
Get users authorized for CUI enclave access

manual.description: HR reconciliation, business justification documentation, and access approval records must be maintained separately

required_documents.contents: Spreadsheet mapping each user account to employee name, department, job role, manager approval, and access justification
Completed and approved access request forms for each user showing management authorization
Documentation of all service accounts, their purpose, owner, and approval for non-interactive access
Evidence of periodic review of all user accounts with management sign-off on continued access

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Missing service accounts in inventory, no HR reconciliation process, undocumented shared mailboxes, guest users not tracked, no formal access request/approval process, stale or disabled accounts not removed, lack of regular access reviews, no clear ownership of service accounts
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export user list 1-2 days before assessment to ensure it's current. Have HR pre-validate the user list. Document any discrepancies between AD and HR systems with explanations. Use Azure AD Access Reviews feature to demonstrate periodic reviews. Ensure all shared mailboxes and service accounts have documented business owners. Create separate reports for different user types (regular, admin, service, guest).

enclave_implementation.description: Use Azure Virtual Desktop with dedicated SharePoint to isolate CUI and reduce CMMC scope
enclave_implementation.benefits: Limits assessment scope to specific Azure resources rather than entire tenant

Objective_Text: processes acting on behalf of authorized users are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires a complete inventory of all service accounts, automated processes, scheduled tasks, and background services that act on behalf of users. Evidence must show service account names, purposes, owners, permissions, creation dates, and last activity. Organizations must demonstrate formal approval processes for service account creation, clear ownership documentation, and regular reviews. System logs must show process execution with user attribution. All automated processes must be traceable to their authorized user or business purpose.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API can inventory service principals, applications, and their permissions. Azure AD audit logs capture service account activities and configurations.

api_endpoints.purpose: List all service accounts and application identities
Retrieve registered applications that use service accounts
Get permissions assigned to service accounts
Audit trail of service account creation and modifications
Service account sign-in activity logs
Retrieve diagnostic settings for process monitoring
Verify Azure Virtual Desktop service principals for CUI enclave
List AVD host pools used for CUI isolation
Get users authorized for CUI enclave access

manual.description: Documentation of service account purposes, ownership, scheduled tasks, and approval records must be maintained outside automated systems

required_documents.contents: Complete list of service accounts with business purpose, technical owner, approval date, and permissions scope
Documentation of all scheduled tasks, automation scripts, and background processes with their associated service accounts
Completed approval forms showing management authorization for each service account creation
Quarterly or annual reviews showing validation of continued need and appropriate permissions for each service account

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Undocumented legacy service accounts, no clear ownership of service accounts, missing approval documentation, service accounts with excessive permissions, no regular review process, scheduled tasks running under user accounts instead of service accounts, no monitoring of service account activities
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Create a service account naming convention to easily identify them in reports. Use Azure AD Privileged Identity Management for service accounts with elevated permissions. Document the separation of duties between request/approval/implementation. Export service principal list before assessment. Have clear mapping between service accounts and the processes/applications they support.

enclave_implementation.description: Use Azure Virtual Desktop with dedicated SharePoint to isolate CUI and reduce CMMC scope
enclave_implementation.benefits: Limits assessment scope to specific Azure resources rather than entire tenant

Objective_Text: devices (and other systems) authorized to connect to the system are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires a complete inventory of all devices authorized to connect to the network including workstations, laptops, mobile devices, servers, IoT devices, and other systems. Evidence must show device names, types, owners, MAC addresses, serial numbers, enrollment status, compliance state, and last connection time. Organizations must demonstrate network access control mechanisms (802.1x, certificates, MDM enrollment), device authentication configurations, and monitoring of unauthorized connection attempts. Device authorization procedures and approval documentation must be maintained.

automated.description: Microsoft Intune and Azure AD provide comprehensive device inventory with compliance states. Network access control logs and device authentication can be exported via APIs.

api_endpoints.purpose: List all Azure AD registered and joined devices
Get all Intune-managed devices with compliance status
Detailed device information including compliance state
Retrieve device compliance policies
Device registration and modification audit logs
Verify Azure Virtual Desktop service principals for CUI enclave
List AVD host pools used for CUI isolation
Get users authorized for CUI enclave access

manual.description: Physical device inventory, network diagrams, and device authorization procedures must be documented separately

required_documents.contents: Complete list of all devices with asset tags, serial numbers, assigned users, and authorization dates
Documentation of how devices are authenticated and authorized to connect (802.1x config, certificate enrollment process)
Policy defining which personal devices can access corporate resources and enrollment requirements
Visual representation showing network segmentation and device access points

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Unmanaged BYOD devices accessing email, missing inventory of IoT/OT devices, no network access control implementation, devices connecting without compliance checks, legacy devices not in Azure AD, no automated blocking of unauthorized devices, incomplete mobile device enrollment
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Use Intune compliance policies with Conditional Access to enforce device compliance. Export device lists from both Azure AD and Intune for complete coverage. Demonstrate live blocking of non-compliant devices during assessment. Have network team ready to show 802.1x logs. Document any legacy devices that cannot be managed by Intune with compensating controls.

enclave_implementation.description: Use Azure Virtual Desktop with dedicated SharePoint to isolate CUI and reduce CMMC scope
enclave_implementation.benefits: Limits assessment scope to specific Azure resources rather than entire tenant

Objective_Text: system access is limited to authorized users

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires evidence that only authorized users can access systems containing CUI. Must demonstrate technical controls preventing unauthorized access including multi-factor authentication, conditional access policies, account lockouts, session timeouts, and access denial logs. Evidence should show user authentication mechanisms, access control lists, role-based permissions, and failed login attempts. Organizations must prove that access controls are enforced consistently across all systems and that unauthorized users are effectively blocked.

automated.description: Azure AD Conditional Access policies, sign-in logs, and authentication reports provide comprehensive evidence of access control enforcement. Microsoft 365 audit logs capture all access attempts.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve all conditional access policies enforcing access restrictions
Get failed sign-in attempts showing blocked unauthorized access
Role-based access control assignments
Security alerts for unauthorized access attempts
Verify Azure Virtual Desktop service principals for CUI enclave
List AVD host pools used for CUI isolation
Get users authorized for CUI enclave access

manual.description: Access control policies and procedures documentation must be maintained separately

required_documents.contents: Formal policy defining who can access what systems, approval processes, and enforcement mechanisms
Documentation showing which users/roles have access to which systems and data
Technical documentation of all conditional access rules and their business justification
Break-glass account procedures for emergency access scenarios

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: No MFA enforcement, legacy authentication protocols still enabled, conditional access policies not covering all apps, guest users with excessive access, no monitoring of failed login attempts, shared accounts still in use, emergency access accounts not properly secured
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Demonstrate live blocking of unauthorized access during assessment. Show conditional access policy simulator results. Have sign-in logs ready showing both successful authorized access and blocked unauthorized attempts. Ensure all legacy authentication is disabled. Document any exceptions with compensating controls. Use Azure AD PIM for privileged access management.

enclave_implementation.description: Use Azure Virtual Desktop with dedicated SharePoint to isolate CUI and reduce CMMC scope
enclave_implementation.benefits: Limits assessment scope to specific Azure resources rather than entire tenant

Objective_Text: system access is limited to processes acting on behalf of authorized users

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that system access is limited to processes acting on behalf of authorized users in a Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This includes, but is not limited to: Implementing Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for managing access to resources and limiting permissions to the minimum necessary, regularly reviewing and auditing user roles and access rights, implementing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and logging and monitoring all access attempts.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides evidence of implemented Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), Azure Active Directory reports, and audit logs for user access.

api_endpoints.purpose: Check user access logs
Verify Azure Virtual Desktop service principals for CUI enclave
List AVD host pools used for CUI isolation
Get users authorized for CUI enclave access

manual.description: Manual documentation must include system access policies, RBAC configuration, MFA implementation details, and audit log review procedures.

required_documents.purpose: Describe the implementation of RBAC
Describe the MFA policy and configuration
Logs showing user access attempts and permissions

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss regular reviews and audits of user roles and access rights, and do not ensure the implementation of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all users.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and Azure AD audit logs, review RBAC configuration documents, and verify MFA enforcement.

enclave_implementation.description: Use Azure Virtual Desktop with dedicated SharePoint to isolate CUI and reduce CMMC scope
enclave_implementation.benefits: Limits assessment scope to specific Azure resources rather than entire tenant

Objective_Text: system access is limited to authorized devices (including other systems)

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessors requires evidence of configuration settings that control access to the system, including IP allow/block lists, conditional access policies, and device compliance checks. They may also request logs showing authorized device activity.

automated.description: Use Azure Active Directory (AAD) reports and APIs to gather information about device compliance and conditional access policies.

Get the device compliance summary report.

Verify Azure Virtual Desktop service principals for CUI enclave

required_documents.contents: List of active Conditional Access Policies with details about required device compliance and access controls.
List of allowed and blocked IP addresses for system access.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss implementing or enforcing device compliance checks, and their conditional access policies may not be sufficiently restrictive.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Ensure that all Conditional Access Policies are properly configured to require multi-factor authentication, approved apps, and compliant devices. Regularly review IP allow/block lists and device compliance reports.

enclave_implementation.description: Use Azure Virtual Desktop with dedicated SharePoint to isolate CUI and reduce CMMC scope
enclave_implementation.benefits: Limits assessment scope to specific Azure resources rather than entire tenant

Objective_Text: the types of transactions and functions that authorized users are permitted to execute are defined

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires clear documentation defining what types of transactions and functions authorized users can perform on CUI systems. Must show role-based function matrices mapping job roles to allowed actions, technical implementation in applications and systems, clear delineation between read/write/delete permissions, administrative versus standard user capabilities, and audit trails proving users can only perform authorized functions. Evidence must demonstrate principle of least privilege implementation.

automated.description: RBAC configurations and permission reports from Azure AD and application systems

api_endpoints.purpose: List all role definitions with associated permissions
Show application-specific roles and allowed functions
Display user role memberships and inherited permissions
Export SharePoint permission levels for CUI repositories
Audit trail of role assignments and permission changes

manual.description: Role definitions and transaction authorization matrices

required_documents.contents: Comprehensive mapping of job functions to system permissions and allowed transactions
How permissions are restricted to minimum necessary for each role
Special controls and approval processes for privileged transactions

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often have generic role assignments without documenting specific allowed transactions. Many cannot demonstrate that technical controls actually enforce the documented permissions. Over-privileged access due to role accumulation without reviews is extremely common. Missing connection between business functions and technical permissions.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Create a demonstration script showing different user roles attempting various transactions. Export role definitions before assessment. Show how a regular user is prevented from admin functions. Have clear documentation linking job titles to technical roles. Demonstrate recent access reviews that removed excess permissions.

Objective_Text: system access is limited to the defined types of transactions and functions for authorized users

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires evidence that system access is strictly limited to only the authorized transaction types and functions assigned to each user role. Must demonstrate role-based access control (RBAC) implementation in M365/Azure AD, showing how permissions align with job functions, proof that users cannot perform unauthorized actions, regular access reviews to validate appropriate permissions, and segregation of duties for sensitive functions. Evidence must include role definitions, permission matrices, access review reports, and live demonstrations of access restrictions.

automated.description: Azure AD roles, Conditional Access policies, and Privileged Identity Management provide comprehensive access control evidence

api_endpoints.purpose: List all role assignments showing user permissions
Export Conditional Access policies restricting access
Show regular access review processes and results
Display application-specific role assignments

manual.description: Role definitions, access matrices, and segregation of duties documentation required

required_documents.contents: Mapping of job functions to M365/Azure roles with authorized transactions per role
Defined incompatible functions and controls preventing single user from having conflicting permissions
Process for quarterly/annual reviews of user permissions with manager approvals

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often fail to document the mapping between job functions and technical permissions. Many cannot demonstrate that access restrictions actually prevent unauthorized actions. Generic role assignments without consideration of least privilege principle is a frequent finding.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Create a permissions test plan showing authorized vs unauthorized actions per role. During assessment, demonstrate access denials for unauthorized functions. Export all role assignments the day before and have justification for each privileged account. Show access review completion evidence from the last quarter.

Objective_Text: information flow control policies are defined

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires evidence that comprehensive information flow control policies are defined for CUI movement within and between systems. Must show documented data flow diagrams with control points, classification of allowed versus prohibited flows, technical policy implementation through DLP and network controls, approval process for new data flows, and regular reviews of flow policies. Policies must address all CUI movement scenarios including email, file transfers, API integrations, and removable media.

automated.description: DLP policy exports and network flow rules provide some technical implementation evidence

api_endpoints.purpose: Export DLP policies defining allowed CUI flows

manual.description: Information flow policies and architectural documentation

required_documents.contents: Comprehensive policy defining all allowed and prohibited CUI data flows
Visual representation of CUI flows between systems, users, and external parties
Mapping of policy requirements to technical controls at each flow point
Analysis of data flow risks and compensating controls

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Most organizations lack comprehensive information flow policies beyond basic DLP rules. Many have network diagrams but not true data flow documentation. Policies often miss API-based data transfers or cloud-to-cloud flows. Failure to define policies before implementing technical controls leads to gaps in coverage.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Have clear, visual data flow diagrams ready - assessors want to see where CUI can and cannot flow. Document all integration points between systems. Show how policy drove technical control selection. Prepare examples of denied flows based on policy. Demonstrate the approval process for new data flow requests.

Objective_Text: methods and enforcement mechanisms for controlling the flow of CUI are defined

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES documentation of methods and enforcement mechanisms for controlling the flow of CUI within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This includes but is not limited to: policies, labels, permissions, and access controls. The documentation should clearly outline how these mechanisms are defined, implemented, monitored, and enforced.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides access to policies, labels, permissions, and access controls. Assessor can use the following endpoints to gather evidence:

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve all policies
Retrieve user permissions
Retrieve group members

manual.description: Manual documentation must include policy and label definitions, permission assignments, and access control lists. This can be found in the Microsoft 365 compliance center, Azure portal, or SharePoint admin center.

required_documents.document: Microsoft 365 Compliance Center - Policies and labels documentation
Azure Portal - Access control lists for resources
SharePoint Admin Center - Group permissions and access controls

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss documenting the enforcement mechanisms, such as alerts or notifications, for policy violations.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API calls and manually review documentation from the compliance center, Azure portal, and SharePoint admin center.

Objective_Text: designated sources and destinations (e.g., networks, individuals, and devices) for CUI within the system and between interconnected systems are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES organizations to provide documentation and evidence that designated sources and destinations (e.g., networks, individuals, and devices) for Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) within the Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate system and between interconnected systems are identified and documented in accordance with AC.L2-3.1.3-c.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides automated identification of networks, individuals, and devices within the Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. API endpoints should be utilized to extract relevant information.

api_endpoints.purpose: List all registered applications and their permissions for system connections
Show service principals and their approved API permissions
Query all network connections and peering relationships

manual.description: Manual documentation must include a detailed inventory of identified sources and destinations for CUI within the Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate system, as well as any interconnected systems.

required_documents.contents: Complete list of all system-to-system connections including API integrations, database links, file transfers, and network connections with approval documentation
Signed approval forms for each system connection showing business justification, data flow, security review, and management authorization
Visual diagrams showing all system interconnections, data types transferred, protocols used, and security controls applied

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss documenting all interconnected systems or fail to properly identify the individuals and devices involved in handling CUI within the Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API, as well as any manually created inventory documents, for review during the assessment.

Objective_Text: authorizations for controlling the flow of CUI are defined

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that organizational authorizations for controlling the flow of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate are clearly defined and documented. This includes but is not limited to roles, permissions, and access controls for users, groups, and applications. The documentation should specify how these authorizations are established, managed, and audited.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides access to user roles and permissions. The API can be used to gather information on role assignments, permission levels, and application-level permissions.

api_endpoints.purpose: Document all application registrations and their API access requirements
Export network connection monitoring data showing active connections

manual.description: Manual documentation must include policies, procedures, and standards related to user roles, permissions, and access controls. This includes a detailed mapping of roles to responsibilities, an overview of the access control model used, and evidence of periodic reviews.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss documenting the rationale behind specific role assignments or access controls, leading to unnecessarily broad permissions. Additionally, some organizations may not perform regular reviews of user roles and access levels.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API for detailed information on roles and permissions. Review manual documentation to ensure it includes the necessary details and evidence of periodic reviews.

Objective_Text: approved authorizations for controlling the flow of CUI are enforced

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires evidence that approved authorizations for controlling CUI data flows are actively enforced through technical controls. Must demonstrate Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies blocking unauthorized CUI transfers, SharePoint/OneDrive external sharing restrictions, email transport rules preventing CUI leakage, approved data flow diagrams with corresponding technical controls, and audit logs showing blocked attempts. Evidence must prove that CUI cannot flow to unauthorized destinations.

automated.description: Microsoft Purview DLP policies, Exchange transport rules, and SharePoint sharing controls enforce CUI flow restrictions

api_endpoints.purpose: Export all DLP policies controlling CUI movement
List mail flow rules blocking CUI transmission
Retrieve DLP violations and blocked attempts

manual.description: CUI flow authorization documentation and approval processes

required_documents.contents: Visual representation of approved CUI flows with technical control points identified
Step-by-step processes for requesting and approving new CUI data flows
Detailed settings for each DLP rule with justification for CUI protection

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often have DLP policies created but not properly scoped to CUI data. Many lack comprehensive coverage across all egress points (email, web uploads, removable media). Failure to test and demonstrate that policies actually block unauthorized transfers is common.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Test DLP policies live during assessment by attempting to send CUI to personal email. Show DLP incident reports from the last 30 days. Demonstrate how blocked attempts are investigated. Have approval documentation ready for any authorized external CUI sharing.

Objective_Text: the duties of individuals requiring separation are defined

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that the duties of individuals requiring separation are clearly defined and documented in written policies or job descriptions. These documents should outline the responsibilities, access levels, and restrictions for these individuals.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve job function/description
Retrieve organization's policies
Show conditional access policies specifically for remote access services
List users authorized for VPN/remote access based on license assignment

manual.description: Manual documentation must include the aforementioned written policies or job descriptions.

required_documents.description: Clear and detailed descriptions of roles, responsibilities, access levels, and restrictions for individuals requiring separation
Policies outlining the rules and procedures for handling sensitive information and managing individuals requiring separation

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss including specific details about access levels, restrictions, and separation duties in their job descriptions or policies.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API to compare the duties of individuals requiring separation with their assigned permissions.

Objective_Text: responsibilities for duties that require separation are assigned to separate individuals

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES documentation that clearly outlines responsibilities for duties requiring separation are assigned to separate individuals in Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This includes but is not limited to: job descriptions, access control policies, and organizational charts that demonstrate the segregation of duties as per AC.L2-3.1.4-b.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides information about access control and roles which can be used to verify segregation of duties.

api_endpoints.purpose: To check user's group membership.
Monitor all remote access authentication events
Track remote desktop and VPN connection metrics over time

manual.description: Manual documentation must include job descriptions, organizational charts, and any other relevant policies or procedures.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss documenting the specific responsibilities and separation of duties in a clear and comprehensive manner.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and compare with the provided job descriptions and organizational chart to ensure proper separation.

Objective_Text: access privileges that enable individuals to exercise the duties that require separation are granted to separate individuals

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that access privileges are granted to separate individuals within the organization's Microsoft 365 environment in a manner that enables individuals to exercise duties requiring separation. This includes but is not limited to: (1) Segregation of duties for system administrators, ensuring no single individual has full control over all critical functions; (2) Least Privilege Principle, granting users only the minimum access necessary to perform their duties; (3) Use of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to manage access and permissions effectively; (4) Regular review and auditing of user roles, access rights, and system logs for any violations or anomalies.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides automated evidence by allowing assessors to check system administrator roles and permissions, user group memberships, access to sensitive data, and audit logs for any violations or unusual activities.

api_endpoints.purpose: Show MFA requirements enforced for remote access
Export session control policies for remote access scenarios

manual.description: Manual documentation must include system administration policies, user access management procedures, role definitions, and evidence of regular audits and reviews.

required_documents.contents: Step-by-step procedures for requesting, approving, provisioning, and revoking remote access including VPN, RDP, and cloud application access
Signed agreements from all remote users acknowledging security requirements, acceptable use, and monitoring

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss implementing the segregation of duties among system administrators, neglecting to enforce the Least Privilege Principle, and failing to regularly review and audit user roles and access rights.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API for automated evidence, and review manual documentation such as policies, procedures, and audit logs for comprehensive evaluation.

Objective_Text: privileged accounts are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that organizations provide evidence demonstrating the identification of privileged accounts within their Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This includes the inventory and documentation of all accounts with elevated permissions or access to sensitive data, including service accounts, administrator accounts, and shared accounts.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides an efficient way to gather account information. The following endpoint is recommended for the purpose: Microsoft Graph API /example (GET)

required_documents.contents: Complete list of all privileged accounts including domain admins, Azure AD Global Admins, application admins, and service accounts with elevated permissions. Must include account purpose, owner, last review date
Mapping of privileged roles to their specific permissions, systems they can access, and business justification for the elevated access

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss including shared accounts or service accounts in their inventory of privileged accounts.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and compare the results with your manually compiled list to ensure completeness. Use Conditional Access reports to show MFA enforcement for all privileged accounts. Export CA policy configurations as evidence.

Objective_Text: access to privileged accounts is authorized in accordance with the principle of least privilege

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES organizations to have a documented and enforced policy that restricts access to privileged accounts in Microsoft 365 to only those individuals who require it for their job functions. This should include the use of least privilege principle, which means providing users with the minimum level of access necessary to perform their tasks effectively. The policy should outline procedures for granting, monitoring, and revoking access, as well as regular audits to ensure compliance.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides access to various aspects of Microsoft 365 including user permissions and privileged account usage. The API can be used to verify if the principle of least privilege is applied correctly.

api_endpoints.purpose: Audit trail of privileged role assignment changes
Access reviews for privileged role assignments
Get Conditional Access policies applied to privileged roles
Verify CA policy enforcement for privileged account sign-ins
List trusted locations for privileged access

manual.description: Manual documentation must include the organization's privileged account policy, access request and approval procedures, and evidence of regular audits.

required_documents.description: Policy outlining least privilege principles for Microsoft 365.
Procedures for requesting, approving, and revoking access to privileged accounts.
Reports demonstrating regular audits of privileged account usage.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss regular audits of privileged account usage and lack specific documentation outlining least privilege principles for Microsoft 365.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from the Azure AD and Microsoft Graph API to verify the principle of least privilege is being applied effectively. Use Conditional Access reports to show MFA enforcement for all privileged accounts. Export CA policy configurations as evidence.

Objective_Text: security functions are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES organizations to provide documentation demonstrating that security functions have been identified in their Microsoft 365 environment. This includes a clear definition and description of each security function, including but not limited to: firewalls, intrusion detection systems (IDS), antivirus software, data loss prevention (DLP) solutions, and encryption tools. The documentation should also outline the specific configuration settings for these security functions.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides programmatic access to security configurations within a Microsoft 365 environment. Assessors can use this API to gather information about configured firewalls, IDS, antivirus software, DLP solutions, and encryption tools.

api_endpoints.purpose: MFA requirements for privileged accounts
Conditional access policies targeting privileged roles

manual.description: Manual documentation must include system configuration documents (SCDs) or security policy documents that clearly define and describe the identified security functions, their specific configurations, and any related settings.

required_documents.contents: Current policy showing access control requirements, approval processes, and implementation procedures
Evidence of periodic access reviews, justifications for continued access, and remediation of inappropriate access

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss providing detailed documentation of all security functions, including configuration settings, which can lead to incomplete assessments.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API or review manual documentation (SCDs/security policy documents) for a comprehensive understanding of the identified security functions and their configurations.

Objective_Text: access to security functions is authorized in accordance with the principle of least privilege

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that access to security functions within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate is authorized in accordance with the principle of least privilege. This includes providing evidence that only necessary users have appropriate levels of access, and that excess privileges are removed when no longer needed. The assessment must demonstrate controls that limit the scope of actions for each user based on their roles and responsibilities.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides automated evidence of user roles and permissions within Microsoft 365. The following endpoint can be used: /me/permissions

api_endpoints.purpose: MFA registration status for admin accounts
Successful sign-in activity for privileged accounts

manual.description: Manual documentation must include user access reviews and role assignment policies that demonstrate adherence to the principle of least privilege.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss documenting and enforcing regular user access reviews to ensure that users only have the necessary permissions.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API for automated evidence, and gather manual documentation of user access reviews and role assignment policies.

Objective_Text: nonsecurity functions are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that non-security functions are clearly identified and documented in a manner that demonstrates they are separate from security functions within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This includes, but is not limited to, the definition of non-security functions, their purpose, and any interaction with security functions.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides data related to the configuration and usage of various functionalities within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate. This information can be used to identify non-security functions.

Objective_Text: users are required to use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that users are required to use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions in Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate, Level 2 assessment. This ensures least privilege and limits potential damage if a user's account is compromised. Specifically, the system should enforce the use of non-administrative accounts for day-to-day tasks, and administrators should be encouraged to implement role-based access control (RBAC) to further limit access to sensitive resources.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides automated evidence of RBAC implementation and user account assignments. The API can be used to verify that users are assigned appropriate roles for their non-administrative tasks.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss implementing or enforcing RBAC, leading to over-privileged user accounts. Additionally, user account management policies may not be clearly defined, documented, or communicated.

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES user functionality within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate, Level 2 environment to be clearly identified and documented. This includes but is not limited to user roles, permissions, access controls, and authentication mechanisms.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides detailed information about user roles, permissions, and authentication mechanisms. Additionally, logs from Azure Active Directory can help identify access controls.

api_endpoints.purpose: Access Controls

manual.description: Manual documentation must include detailed descriptions and diagrams of user roles, permissions, and access controls.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss documenting user role responsibilities and the rationale behind granting certain permissions.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and Azure Active Directory logs, and review manual documentation for completeness.

Objective_Text: system management functionality is identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that the system management functionality for Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate, Level 2 is identified and documented. This includes but is not limited to the identification of system configuration settings, user account management, software deployment, patch management, and security configuration. The documentation should clearly outline the tools, processes, and procedures used for these functions.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides access to various system management functionality. For example, using the Microsoft Graph API, an assessor can retrieve information about user accounts, software installations, security configurations, and more.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve user account information
Retrieve device information

manual.description: Manual documentation must include system management policies, procedures, and guidelines. This could include system configuration settings, user account management policies, software deployment procedures, patch management processes, and security configuration standards.

required_documents.purpose: Document the system configuration settings and their rationale
Document the procedures for creating, managing, and deactivating user accounts
Document the procedures for deploying software to systems in the environment
Document the processes for applying patches and updates to the system
Document the security configuration standards for the Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss documenting the rationale behind certain system management decisions, which can lead to inconsistencies and potential security vulnerabilities.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and review manual documentation to ensure all required information is included.

Objective_Text: user functionality is separated from system management functionality

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants:
Assessor REQUIRES that user functionality is clearly separated from system management functionality within the Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This separation should be implemented in a way that ensures no unauthorized access to system management functions by regular users, and vice versa. Evidence must demonstrate: 
1. User interfaces are distinctly different from administrative interfaces.
2. Separation of duties is enforced, preventing a single user from having control over both user functionality and system management functionality.
3. Access controls are in place to prevent unauthorized access to system management functions.
4. Logging and auditing mechanisms record any changes made to system management functions.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides access to various system management functions and their corresponding logs. The logs can be used to verify separation of duties and access controls.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access
List role assignments showing privileged access controls

manual.description: Manual documentation must include the design of user interfaces, administrative interfaces, separation of duties policy, access control policy, and logs/audit trails.

required_documents.contents: Document showing manual review of user access rights, justifications for privileged access, manager approvals, and any access changes made
Organization-specific security settings, deviations from Microsoft baselines with business justifications, and approval signatures

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss implementing a clear visual distinction between user interfaces and administrative interfaces, and may lack detailed documentation regarding the implementation of separation of duties and access controls.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API for system management functions logs and audit trails to demonstrate compliance.

Objective_Text: unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources is prevented

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES verification that unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources in a Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment is prevented. This includes but is not limited to: network file shares, email, instant messaging, collaboration platforms, and other shared resources. Evidence should demonstrate the implementation of controls such as access controls, data loss prevention (DLP) policies, user education, and monitoring.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides data for network file shares, email, and instant messaging. Log analytics can be used to monitor activity and DLP policies.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access

manual.description: Manual documentation must include policies, procedures, training records, and examples of monitoring and incident response.

required_documents.document: Network File Share Access Control Policy
required_documents.purpose: Describe access controls for network file shares.
Document DLP policies, including rules and exceptions.
Show evidence of user education on data security.
Describe the process for handling information security incidents.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss implementing and enforcing strict access controls, properly configuring DLP policies, and providing regular user education on data security best practices.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and Log Analytics to demonstrate the implementation of controls. Review documentation for policies, procedures, training records, and incident response.

Objective_Text: publicly accessible system components are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that the organization provides documentation or evidence demonstrating the identification of publicly accessible system components within their Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This should include a detailed inventory of all externally-facing assets, including websites, applications, APIs, and any other system components that are publicly available.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides access to various assets within the Microsoft 365 environment. It can be used to gather information about publicly accessible sites, applications, and APIs.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access
List role assignments showing privileged access controls

manual.description: Manual documentation must include a detailed inventory of publicly accessible system components, including URLs for websites and applications, API endpoint details (if applicable), and any other relevant information.

required_documents.contents: Document showing manual review of user access rights, justifications for privileged access, manager approvals, and any access changes made
Organization-specific security settings, deviations from Microsoft baselines with business justifications, and approval signatures

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss identifying less common publicly accessible components such as hidden APIs or obscure webpages.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and manually review documentation for any missed components.

Objective_Text: subnetworks for publicly accessible system components are physically or logically separated from internal networks

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires evidence that subnetworks for publicly accessible system components are physically or logically separated from internal networks handling CUI. Must demonstrate DMZ implementation with proper firewall rules, network segmentation validated through documentation and testing, no direct routes between public-facing systems and CUI networks, regular penetration testing of segmentation controls, and monitoring of cross-zone traffic. Evidence must prove isolation is effective and maintained.

automated.description: Network security group rules, Azure Firewall policies, and network topology validation

api_endpoints.purpose: Query network topology and segmentation configuration
Export NSG rules showing network isolation
Retrieve firewall metrics and blocked connection attempts
Get network security assessments and recommendations

manual.description: Network architecture documentation and segmentation validation

required_documents.contents: Visual showing DMZ, internal networks, CUI zones with all interconnection points
Detailed rules showing what traffic is allowed between network segments
Third-party validation of network segmentation effectiveness
Process for requesting and approving firewall rule changes

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often have basic DMZ but lack proper isolation from CUI networks. Many have firewall rules that are too permissive or have undocumented exceptions. Missing regular validation of segmentation effectiveness through testing. Failure to monitor for unauthorized cross-zone communications is common.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Show network diagram with traffic flows during assessment. Demonstrate that public-facing systems cannot directly access CUI. Export and explain critical firewall rules. Have penetration test results ready showing segmentation was validated. Run traceroute to prove isolation. Show alerts for any attempted cross-zone violations.

Objective_Text: network communications traffic is denied by default

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that network communications traffic is denied by default in Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate, Level 2 assessment. This involves configuring settings to block all incoming and outgoing traffic by default, with specific exceptions granted for necessary services or applications. The firewall should be configured to monitor and log all attempts at communication that are blocked.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides insights into network security group rules and firewall configurations. An example endpoint could be '/network/firewalls' to get details about the configured firewall rules.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access
List role assignments showing privileged access controls

manual.description: Manual documentation must include the firewall configuration settings, access control lists (ACLs), and any relevant network security policies.

required_documents.contents: Document showing manual review of user access rights, justifications for privileged access, manager approvals, and any access changes made
Organization-specific security settings, deviations from Microsoft baselines with business justifications, and approval signatures

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss configuring specific exceptions for necessary services or applications, leading to denial of legitimate traffic. Also, incomplete or outdated firewall rules can pose a risk.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Defender for Cloud or Azure Security Center that detail network security group rules and firewall configurations.

Objective_Text: network communications traffic is allowed by exception

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that the organization demonstrates controls for network communications traffic allowed by exception in compliance with SC.L2-3.13.6-b. This should include evidence of policies and procedures that govern exceptions to standard network communication traffic rules, as well as documentation of exceptions, their purpose, and duration. Additionally, evidence should be provided showing the methods used for monitoring and controlling such exceptions.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides detailed network traffic logs and policies. This includes information on allowed exceptions, network flows, and the associated policies.

api_endpoints.purpose: To retrieve network policy configurations
Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access

manual.description: Manual documentation must include policy and procedure documents, as well as logs or reports of exception traffic and the associated approvals.

required_documents.purpose: To demonstrate control over network traffic
To provide evidence of exceptions to standard network traffic rules and their associated approvals

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss providing detailed documentation for the purposes, duration, and approvals related to exception traffic.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API endpoints related to network traffic policies and exceptions, as well as manually review policy and procedure documents for details on exception traffic.

Objective_Text: remote devices are prevented from simultaneously establishing non-remote connections with the system and communicating via some other connection to resources in external networks (i.e., split tunneling)

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that the organization has implemented measures to prevent remote devices from simultaneously establishing non-remote connections with the system and communicating via some other connection to resources in external networks (i.e., split tunneling) within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate Level 2 environment.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides evidence of policies enforced related to split tunneling. This includes configuration settings for Conditional Access policies, Intune policies, and network connection security rules.

manual.description: Manual documentation must include screenshots or configuration files of relevant policies and settings, such as Conditional Access policies, Intune policies, and network connection security rules.

required_documents.contents: Detailed procedures showing how this control is implemented, responsible parties, and validation methods
Recent evidence demonstrating control effectiveness, testing results, and continuous monitoring data

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss implementing and enforcing split tunneling prevention at the device configuration level through Intune policies.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API calls, and review configuration settings in the Azure portal for Conditional Access policies, Intune policies, and network connection security rules.

Objective_Text: cryptographic mechanisms intended to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES documentation of cryptographic mechanisms implemented within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment that are intended to prevent unauthorized disclosure of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). This should include details about the specific algorithms, key management processes, and encryption standards used for data protection.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides details about implemented encryption methods and data protection settings.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access
List role assignments showing privileged access controls

manual.description: Manual documentation must include details about encryption algorithms, key management processes, and encryption standards used for data protection.

required_documents.contents: Document showing manual review of user access rights, justifications for privileged access, manager approvals, and any access changes made
Organization-specific security settings, deviations from Microsoft baselines with business justifications, and approval signatures

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss the provision of detailed documentation on the encryption mechanisms implemented, especially when relying heavily on Microsoft's built-in encryption features.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft 365 Compliance Manager and review the 'Data Protection' and 'Encryption' sections for relevant information.

Objective_Text: alternative physical safeguards intended to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that alternative physical safeguards intended to prevent unauthorized disclosure of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) in a Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment are identified, documented, and implemented. These safeguards should include measures such as locked storage areas, restricted access to physical facilities, and monitoring of personnel with access to the areas where CUI is stored.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides information about the implemented access controls and permissions within Microsoft 365. This includes details about who has access to which resources, and the level of access they have.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access
List role assignments showing privileged access controls

manual.description: Manual documentation must include policies and procedures related to the physical safeguards in place, as well as evidence of their implementation.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss the implementation of strict access controls and monitoring of personnel who have physical access to areas where CUI is stored.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and review manual documentation for evidence of alternative physical safeguards.

Objective_Text: either cryptographic mechanisms or alternative physical safeguards are implemented to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI during transmission

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that for SC.L2-3.13.8-c, during transmission of CUI, Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate implementation demonstrates cryptographic mechanisms or alternative physical safeguards to prevent unauthorized disclosure. Evidence should include the use of Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption at minimum, with additional details about encryption keys and key management, and/or physical measures such as secure transmission facilities.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides access to Transmission Security (TLS) configuration details and encryption key management information.

manual.description: Manual documentation must include a description of physical safeguards employed for secure transmission facilities, if applicable.

required_documents.contents: Detailed procedures showing how this control is implemented, responsible parties, and validation methods
Recent evidence demonstrating control effectiveness, testing results, and continuous monitoring data

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss to provide details about encryption key management and alternative physical safeguards, if any.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API for TLS configuration, encryption key management, and relevant manual documentation.

Objective_Text: a period of inactivity to terminate network connections associated with communications sessions is defined

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that a defined period of inactivity is configured to terminate network connections associated with communications sessions for Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate, Level 2. The defined period of inactivity should be set according to the organization's security policy and best practices, but must not exceed 1 hour. This includes Terminal Services, Remote Desktop Services, Virtual Private Network (VPN) connections, and any other remote access technologies.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides automated evidence for checking the presence of a defined period of inactivity for terminating network connections associated with communications sessions. The API can be used to retrieve configuration settings and logs related to the specified network connections.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access

manual.description: Manual documentation must include network connection configuration settings, log files showing the period of inactivity, and any relevant system documentation related to network connection termination.

required_documents.contents: Document showing manual review of user access rights, justifications for privileged access, manager approvals, and any access changes made
Organization-specific security settings, deviations from Microsoft baselines with business justifications, and approval signatures

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss documenting or implementing a defined period of inactivity for remote access technologies, leading to potential security risks due to open connections.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and review system logs to verify the presence of a defined period of inactivity.

Objective_Text: network connections associated with communications sessions are terminated at the end of the sessions

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires evidence that all network connections associated with CUI communications sessions are properly terminated when sessions end. Must demonstrate automatic session timeout configurations, proper TCP connection termination, VPN disconnect on idle, RDP/SSH session management, and audit logs showing session terminations. Evidence must prove orphaned connections cannot persist and potentially be hijacked.

automated.description: Session timeout policies and connection logs from various Microsoft services

api_endpoints.purpose: Show session timeout configurations for authentication
Export Conditional Access session control policies
Retrieve network flow logs showing connection terminations
Audit successful sign-ins and session durations

manual.description: Session management configurations and timeout policies

required_documents.contents: Timeout values for different connection types, idle termination rules, re-authentication requirements
Firewall rules, VPN settings, and TCP timeout configurations
RDP/SSH hardening with specific session termination controls

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often configure web application timeouts but miss network-level session controls. Many lack comprehensive session termination across all access methods (VPN, RDP, cloud apps). Failure to validate that sessions actually terminate and cannot be reused is common.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Demonstrate session timeout live during assessment - show automatic disconnection. Export session logs showing proper terminations. Test that terminated sessions cannot be resumed. Have all timeout configurations documented by connection type. Show monitoring for abnormal session durations.

Objective_Text: network connections associated with communications sessions are terminated after the defined period of inactivity

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that network connections associated with communications sessions in a Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment are terminated after a defined period of inactivity. This includes but is not limited to: a) VPN connections b) Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) connections c) email connections d) file transfer connections e) chat and collaboration platform connections. The defined period of inactivity should be less than 4 hours, and the termination process should be automatic.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides automated evidence for checking the termination of network connections. It can be used to verify VPN, RDP, email, and file transfer connection settings.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access
List role assignments showing privileged access controls

required_documents.contents: Document showing manual review of user access rights, justifications for privileged access, manager approvals, and any access changes made
Organization-specific security settings, deviations from Microsoft baselines with business justifications, and approval signatures

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss proper configuration of automatic termination for all types of network connections, or have a defined period of inactivity exceeding 4 hours.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API, and review manual documentation related to network connection policies and logs.

Objective_Text: cryptographic keys are established whenever cryptography is employed

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that in compliance with SC.L2-3.13.10-a of CMMC for Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate Level 2 assessment, organizations must establish cryptographic keys whenever cryptography is employed. Evidence should demonstrate that encryption keys are generated and used consistently across all relevant applications and services in the environment.

Organization-specific security settings, deviations from Microsoft baselines with business justifications, and approval signatures

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss verifying that encryption keys are consistently generated and used across all relevant applications and services in the environment.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API to demonstrate key management and encryption configuration, and review documentation from Microsoft 365 admin center for additional evidence.

Objective_Text: cryptographic keys are managed whenever cryptography is employed

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that organizations demonstrate the management of cryptographic keys whenever cryptography is employed in Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This includes policies for key creation, rotation, revocation, and backup. Evidence should also show secure storage and distribution mechanisms, as well as access controls and auditing mechanisms.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides evidence of key management policies and practices. This includes details about key rotation, backup, and access controls.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access

manual.description: Manual documentation must include detailed procedures for key management, as well as logs showing implementation of these procedures.

required_documents.purpose: To demonstrate the organization's procedures for managing cryptographic keys
To show implementation of key management procedures

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss providing detailed evidence about the secure storage and distribution mechanisms for cryptographic keys.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API endpoints to provide evidence of key management policies and practices.

Objective_Text: FIPS-validated cryptography is employed to protect the confidentiality of CUI

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that FIPS-validated cryptography is implemented and configured for protecting the confidentiality of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This includes, but is not limited to, using FIPS 140-2 or higher validated encryption algorithms for encrypting CUI, implementing FIPS-validated key management solutions, and ensuring that all relevant services and applications are configured accordingly.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides access to the encryption settings and configurations for various services within the Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. Assessors can use this API to verify FIPS-validation status, encryption algorithms in use, and other relevant configuration details.

api_endpoints.purpose: Retrieve conditional access policies controlling user access
List role assignments showing privileged access controls

manual.description: Manual documentation must include system logs, configuration files, and documentation demonstrating the FIPS validation status of encryption algorithms in use and their application within the Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment.

required_documents.contents: Document showing manual review of user access rights, justifications for privileged access, manager approvals, and any access changes made
Organization-specific security settings, deviations from Microsoft baselines with business justifications, and approval signatures

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss validating and documenting that all relevant services and applications are configured to use FIPS-validated cryptography for protecting CUI.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Compliance Manager, which provides a summary of compliance status across various security controls, including the use of FIPS-validated cryptography.

Objective_Text: collaborative computing devices are identified

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that a complete inventory of collaborative computing devices (such as laptops, desktops, tablets, and mobile phones) used within the organization's Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment is identified, including their configuration details and assigned users.

assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API or other relevant tools, and combine them with manual documentation to complete the evidence.

Objective_Text: collaborative computing devices provide indication to users of devices in use

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that collaborative computing devices (e.g., shared laptops, tablets) within Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment provide a visual indication to users when another user is currently using the device. This can be demonstrated through system prompts or status indicators on the device.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss providing clear and obvious visual indications, making it difficult for users to determine whether a device is in use or not.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and ensure they include the details of devices with visual indicators.

Objective_Text: remote activation of collaborative computing devices is prohibited

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES organizations to have a policy in place that prohibits the remote activation of collaborative computing devices within their Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. The policy should clearly state that all devices, including but not limited to laptops, desktops, and mobile devices, must be manually activated by an authorized user physically present at the device location.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss updating their policies to reflect the latest security requirements, or they do not have a clear policy on remote activation.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API and review the organization's IT policies for compliance.

Objective_Text: use of mobile code is controlled

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor requires evidence that mobile code is strictly controlled to prevent unauthorized execution in CUI environments. Must show application control policies blocking unauthorized code, PowerShell execution policies and logging, macro security settings in Office, browser controls for JavaScript/ActiveX, and code signing requirements. Evidence must demonstrate both preventive controls and detection of attempted mobile code execution.

automated.description: Application control policies, script execution monitoring, and macro security settings

api_endpoints.purpose: List installed software and identify unauthorized code
Retrieve AppLocker or WDAC policies

PowerShell controls are frequently inadequate. Failure to address all mobile code types (not just traditional executables) causes assessment failures.

Have logs of blocked execution attempts from the last 30 days. Test browser controls for ActiveX/Java blocking.

Objective_Text: use of mobile code is monitored

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES that the organization demonstrates monitoring and control of the use of mobile code within the Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate environment. This includes the implementation of policies to restrict or allow specific types of mobile code, logging and reviewing the execution of mobile code, and documenting any exceptions.

assessor_guidance.common_gaps: Organizations often miss implementing specific policies for controlling the use of mobile code, not regularly reviewing logs related to mobile code execution, and failing to document exceptions or incidents related to mobile code.
assessor_guidance.assessor_tips: Export reports from Microsoft Graph API, review policy documentation, and check incident reports to demonstrate compliance with SC.L2-3.13.13-b.

Objective_Text: use of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies is controlled

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES organizations using Microsoft 365 GCC Moderate to demonstrate compliance with SC.L2-3.13.14-a by providing evidence that Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies are controlled within the environment. This includes policies, procedures, and technical configurations that secure VoIP usage in accordance with NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2 requirements.

Objective_Text: use of Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies is monitored

assessor_guidance.what_assessor_wants: Assessor REQUIRES documentation demonstrating that Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technologies used within the organization are monitored to ensure appropriate usage and security. This includes evidence of policies, procedures, and technical controls in place for monitoring VoIP activities. The assessment will consider both automated and manual sources of evidence.

automated.description: Microsoft Graph API provides logs and reports related to VoIP activities within Microsoft Teams. Assessor may request exports of relevant reports as evidence.
